issues.description: The method Milkable.messageOnMilk() has conflicting return types across artifacts. The problem statement/UML and task text specify messageOnMilk() should return a String (a message like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked") (see problem_statement.md lines 51-53 and 92-95). In the solution repository, the Milkable interface declares messageOnMilk() as returning boolean (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java line 5), and the Seal and Goat implementations print the message and return boolean (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java line 19 and src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java line 15). The template Main.java calls System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk()), which expects a String return (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 30-32). This mismatch (String expected by problem/template vs boolean provided by solution) will confuse students and can cause compilation/type errors or incorrect test behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent with the problem statement: change the Milkable interface method signature to `String messageOnMilk()` and update Seal and Goat to return the message string (e.g., `return "Seal " + getName() + " is milked";`) instead of printing and returning boolean. Update any call sites (e.g., Main or tests) to consume and/or print the returned String. Alternatively, if the teaching intent is to return boolean and print inside implementations, update the problem statement and template to explicitly document the boolean return and side-effect printing, but aligning the solution to the documented String-returning API is recommended.
